utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Madam Registrar, can you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-05-88/2-PT, The Prosecutor versus Zdravko Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, I would like to confirm that you are receiving interpretation and can understand me. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you. I understand you, and I'm hearing you quite clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you have any difficulties at any point in hearing me, please let me know immediately. May I have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Peter McCloskey with Rupert Elderkin and Janet Stewart for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And I note Mr. Tolimir is present, self-represented. Before we begin, I have one preliminary matter, Mr. Tolimir. At the last Status Conference, it was your first appearance as a self-represented accused, and you were given at that time what I would as some latitude to express personal religious beliefs through the prayer at the beginning of the conversation. However, you have elected, Mr. Tolimir, to represent yourself in a court proceeding, and you must conform your conduct to that context. While your religious beliefs are certainly fully respected here, so to must be the proper decorum and procedures of this Tribunal. So from now on, I would ask you to refrain from such interventions and restrict yourself to matters appropriate to the court proceeding. If you wish to offer prayers in relation to the proceedings, please do so outside the courtroom before or after they commence, or else silently to yourself. I'm sure you will understand and cooperate with me on this. I'm going to move, then, to the substantive matters for this afternoon. This is the second Status Conference in this matter. And under the Rules, the Status Conference purposes are clear to organise exchanges regarding preparations for trial, to look at the status of the case, and, importantly, to allow you, Mr. Tolimir, to raise any issues including issues related to your mental or physical condition, treatment, at the UNDU, et cetera. As has been our practice, I'll begin by going over the few - I have very few - agenda items this afternoon; and then both the Prosecution and you, Mr. Tolimir, can raise any issues that you wish to after that. I'm going to begin with a very minor matter. I just wanted to have confirmed on the record the practice which is already in place relating to filing deadlines, in light of the fact that the accused is self-represented at the moment and that requires a translation of documents. As has been the case to date, any filing deadlines applicable to the Prosecution, Mr. McCloskey, will commence when the translation of any submission made by Mr. Tolimir is filed. So it would be filing date of the translation. Similarly, Mr. Tolimir, the deadlines for you will run from the date of service, or attempted service, of the translation of the documents. For the purpose of the registry and the Chamber and the Prosecution, the date of that service or attempted service will be determined based on the proces-verbals which are currently being filed from time to time indicating the dates of service. So I don't need any submissions on this point. I simply wanted to confirm that point on the record. Now, if we can move, then, to the probably the most substantive matter I wanted to deal with this afternoon, and that is pending motions in this case. And let me say, before dealing with the two motions I was going to discuss originally, I am aware, Mr. Tolimir, that you have filed a new submission. I believe it was filed yesterday. However, I have not received a formal translation of that submission, nor obviously has the Prosecution or the registry, if they're complicated, had an opportunity to review it as well, to receive a translation and review it. So I will not be addressing that submission today. The normal time-lines will run, and we will deal with it if it requires decision after the recess. However, I have been advised that it may relate, one again, to the issue of language, which we're going to be addressing this afternoon. So I would note that, in the absence of new material, you can anticipate similar disposition in the matter as will be discussed shortly. There are two main motions pending that I want to mention. First, there have been preliminary motions filed under Rule 72, that was filed by you, Mr. Tolimir, within the deadline set, on the 30th of October, with a translation being filed on the 7th November. Prosecution has replied to that motion on the 21st of November. I can indicate that the decision on those motions -- on that motion and those objections will be rendered shortly prior to the recess. So you can expect that to be delivered by the Trial Chamber in due course. I move, then, to the motion to the Pre-Trial Chamber and the Registrar concerning assistance in appointing a legal advisor, disclosure of material in a language that the accused understands, and notification of special Defence on charges in the indictment, which was a motion filed by Mr. Tolimir on the 16th of November, with the translation filed on the 20th of November. The Prosecution has responded to that on December 4th, as well as the registry has made a submission in relation to it on the 7th of December. I intend to deal orally with that motion, today, Mr. Tolimir. You have raised, essentially, two main issues in this motion; one relating to the appointment of a legal advisor, and the second relating to the service of documents and the language and script in which they are being served. On the first issue of the appointment of a legal advisor, I need to reiterate that the primary responsibility for these matters, Mr. Tolimir, rests with the registry. The Trial Chamber's involvement would arise if there is a specific decision taken, for example, that you want to bring to us for review. However, from looking through your filings carefully, as well as those of the -- the registry, I'm satisfied that that is not the case here as of yet. Now, it is evident to me that are ongoing discussions between you and the registry on this very important matter, and I would encourage you to continue to liaise with them on it. I would also urge the registry to make its best efforts to try and resolve the matter of an appointment of a legal advisor as soon as possible. It is obviously a very crucial matter for the preparation of trial proceedings. However, beyond that, there is nothing raised in this motion which is properly before the Trial Chamber at this time, so there is no need for any particular decision on that first issue. But, again, Mr. Tolimir, I encourage you to continue to discuss the matter with the registry, and I do recognise that this is an important matter for you. I move, then, to the second issue, that is raised in this motion, which is the language and script of the documents that are being served. Mr. Tolimir, we're going to close this chapter today. At the last Status Conference, I left the door open for you. We discussed this matter extensively, and I left the door open for to you come back to me on this issue, but I did so with the hope that you would either reflect on it and change your position, as I encouraged you to do, or that you would provide something by way of a clear explanation and support for the position that you're taking. But, unfortunately, you have done neither. I have filings by the registry which evidence your continuing refusal to accept documents which are not in, as you term it, Serbian and the Cyrillic script; and, further, your motion provides no explanation beyond a mere assertion that you don't understand the Latin script. You are correct, Mr. Tolimir, there is a right to receive relevant material in this Tribunal in a language you can understand, but this does not translate into a right for an accused, regardless of his or her background, education, experience, to come before this Tribunal and demand the production of documents in any language or script that he or she chooses. As I explained last time, in great detail, the right centres on understanding, not on preference. For your request to be entertained, Mr. Tolimir, there must be something in the record beyond mere assertions to cast doubt on your ability to understand material being provided to you in these proceedings. And here the record simply does not raise such doubts; and, in fact, it supports the opposite conclusion. I'm just going to, by way of summary, highlight some of the points in the record to which I'm referring. You were educated in the former Yugoslavia where in accordance with the submission of the registry, of 18th July, and acknowledged by you to me at the Status Conference, the Roman script was taught in the school system. When you first appeared before this Tribunal, the indictment was served upon you in B/C/S and the Latin script, and you acknowledged to me, on the 4th of June, that you had, and I'm quoting here, "received a copy in a language I understand two days ago, and I have had time to read it and look through it." On the basis of that same material, Mr. Tolimir, you were able, within the time limits that were set, to prepare and submit preliminary objections to the indictment, and the arguments you have advanced clearly indicate an understanding of the content of that indictment. When I put direct questions to you, Mr. Tolimir, you have given me inconsistent answers on the issue of your understanding of the Latin script. These have ranged from "I don't understand it," to "I don't understand sufficiently," to it being a language in which you cannot read it quickly, to it being less understandable. You have even pointed to medical circumstances in 1983 which required you to relearn part of the language, but you have not submitted anything to me in support of that. And I also have noted, Mr. Tolimir, the Prosecution filed, on the 10th of October, in response your request for an extension of time, with their response they provided examples of documents dating from the period of 1992 to 1995, which were in Serbian in the Latin script, and they were either signed by you, or sent to you in your official capacity with the army at that time. And I must note on the record, Mr. Tolimir, those documents were filed, and I have also seen similar documents in the course of sitting on the Popovic et al trial. For me to accept your assertion of lack of understanding, I would have to believe that you are -- you as an intelligent man, which you are, as a high-ranking army official at that time in the middle of a war, that you are communicating, sending out, receiving documents in a language you didn't understand. I don't accept that, Mr. Tolimir. Therefore, based on all the material on the record, examples of which I have given, I do not doubt, rather, I'm positively satisfied that you are able to read and understand the material that's being provided to you in B/C/S in the Latin script. I'm further convinced that the sole basis for your objections is that these materials do not correspond precisely to the official national language in Serbia. But as I stated to you last time, Mr. Tolimir, that is not a basis upon which I would make a determination to -- to defer the resources, the precious resources, the translation resources of the Tribunal to assign them the task of translating of these documents. Therefore, your motion of the 20th November, that's the date of the filing of the translation, is denied in so far as the request for language document service is concerned. As I've said, Mr. Tolimir, we are closing this chapter today, but I want you to be perfectly clear about one thing. The charges against you are extremely grave, and the case is a very complex one. You have been given time, and we have exhaustively considered the issue of these documents. Without prejudice, of course, to any objections you have made on jurisdiction in the indictment, trial preparation in this case needs to proceed. That cannot even begin to take place in real terms without regard -- you having regard to the evidence which you have so far refused to accept. It's an intolerable situation and one which the Trial Chamber cannot allow to continue indefinitely. I'm urging you, one more time, over the next short period, to reconsider the stance you have taken for the next week or so and to accept the service of documents on the next occasion. Failing that, Mr. Tolimir, you need to be clear that you will be leaving the Trial Chamber no option but to take action, and in particular to reconsider the issue of your self-representations considering that your conduct at this time is blocking entirely the proper and expeditious trial preparation. To finish the matter, Mr. Tolimir, the choice is yours. I'm going to move, then, to the third issue that I had on my agenda, which involved you, Mr. McCloskey. Last time, we spoke about the disclosure situation with reference to Rule 66(A)(ii). And without obviously addressing the question of service, acceptance of service, let's put it that way, I wonder if you are able to update me at all as to the status of the disclosure of the Rule 66(A)(ii) materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We are prepared to provide that material as soon as -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We've got that material. It's ready to go. It came back once, but it can be sent again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: So all of the material that we discussed last time, which you were putting together, you have attempted service of those materials. Is that correct? Is there anything outstanding, I suppose, is what I am looking to see. If the materials were accepted, would that constitute a complete package of disclosure as required?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I want to double-check that, Madam President, but we should be close; though, there's -- we're going to need a fair amount of audio statements and other things. So I will need to double-check that, but we're very close. When it comes back at us, that's the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: I would ask you -- thank you, Mr. McCloskey. I would ask you to do that, to double-check, as soon as you can, and to put yourself in a position where you are able to confirm that that material has been or is in the position of being disclosable; and then we'll take it from is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All the material is on the EDS, so we have the -- we the ability to provide the indexes to the EDS just like that, and so it is just a matter of getting the ability to do that. I have introduced myself to the General today, and perhaps we can work out some sort of a situation where he will help avail himself of that option to go on the electronic disclosure system where this material is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. McCloskey, and I would encourage you to continue to pursue those discussions and that avenue, so that next time we can perhaps complete that issue in terms of the record. Mr. Tolimir, do you have any questions you wish to raise or issues or comments on this disclosure question related to Rule 66(A)(ii).

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have several matters I wish to raise in relation to what you've just indicated. First, I wish to greet everyone present, and I would like to refer back to everything you have said, not only to what the Prosecutor has just stated. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tolimir. I'm happy to hear you on the issue of 66(A)(ii), or if you had any -- any issues pertaining to the filing deadline that I outlined initially. However, on the issue of languages, Mr. Tolimir, I have heard extensive submissions. We've had discussions about that issue both in writing and orally, and I have now ruled on the matter. So I don't wish to revisit that particular issue. If you wish to raise anything, however, regarding disclosure materials under 66(A)(ii), the matter just discussed with the Prosecution, I'm happy to hear you on that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. All the problems are related to the language, and the problem of the language has to be discussed before everything else can be resolved. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tolimir. You have my ruling on that and my comments on that, so we will proceed on to the next issue. For me, the only remaining issue that I wanted to raise this afternoon was the question of your health, Mr. Tolimir. Now, as always, I'm prepared to discuss this, if you prefer, in private session; otherwise, we can discuss it in publicly, but it is entirely up to you. Would you like to proceed in private session for a discussion of any health issues you might wish to raise or general issues of your conditions of the UNDU? Would you like to go to private session?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. There is no need to move into private session because the registry has been manipulating my health, and I wish my health to be publicly discussed, but after we have discussed the earlier matters that the Trial Chamber seems to be avoiding all the time. And before these matters are solved, nothing further can be dealt with. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I think I have made myself very clear, and I don't think my comments this afternoon could be classified as avoidance in any respect. So, we are not going to discuss the language issue again. However, I would very much like to give you the opportunity to raise anything to do with your health. In particular, I want to know if there's any particular things in terms of your conditions at the UNDU that you wanted specifically to raise with me. So I would appreciate, if you wanted to raise those, that you do so at this time.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the accused, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Tolimir. You need your microphone on. There, that's better. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish the discussion on my health to be in public session and not in private session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: That's fine. So we are in public session. Are there any particular matters that you want to raise regarding your health, your treatment, anything that you wish to bring to the Trial Chamber's attention, to my attention?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I wish to state that you, as the Trial Chamber, never respond to any of my filings. Ever since my arrival here, none of my requests were met by you, including my request that I addressed to you and the registry on several occasions, with regard to the infringement of my discretionary rights and my abuse in detention from the moment I was arrested to this very day. My health is excellent, and all the medical checkups have proved that. The last two medical checkups have shown that my pressure is good. The top ceiling is 130 -- the top one being 130, and the lower one being 85 or 90. This is the situation with regard to my pressure. Without the administration of any medication, and with my active physical exercise, in view of my age, I believe my blood pressure is excellent. However, the registry has been insisting upon informing the public that my death is imminent and that my health is in a very bad condition, and there's really no reason for that whatsoever, for such information to be divulged. I wrote in my filing that this was calculated with a view to depriving me of my self-representation, as is your position not to serve documents upon me in my own language and in the script I understand. This is also geared toward depriving me of my right to defend myself. The registry and UNDU are purportedly taking care of my health for the sake of the public; whereas, in reality, they're doing everything in their power to cause my health to deteriorate. My cell is under 24-hour camera surveillance. There is a light on in my cell even at night, and the guards insist upon waking me up every half-hour to check up on my health and on my situation in the cell. Every working day, from the moment I was arrested to this very date, and that's six months, I seem to be going through such an experience as if I were sleeping in a train compartment. Everybody keeps waking me up; whereas, the public portrayal of my situation is that of my health being perfect. My wife wanted to bring me three different assortments of tea, since I don't take any medication. Now they've prohibited me from drinking camomile tea, herbal teas that would help improve my urinary problems that I have had for several years now. This is contrary to all rules governing human rights, particularly of individuals held in detention who have not yet been convicted. They want to drug me with medication, the origin of which I'm not aware of; whereas, they prohibit me from drinking teas that I'm perfectly familiar with. In addition to all this, I am in excellent health, regardless of the medication needed. But what I need is to be able to prepare my Defence and to given all the necessary pre-conditions for preparing my Defence out of my cell, out of detention. All the rights that you have stem from the rights of the accused under the Statute. Articles 20 and 21 provide that all the original rights are vested with the accused. The accused is the one who has the rights that everybody else has to respect; however, you, as the Presiding Judge of the Trial Chamber, do not respect them. The Prosecution does not respect them by serving upon me material in a language that I don't understand. The registry does not respect them, as they -- they consider me to have been preparing for my Defence for these past six years; whereas, I have not received a single document aside from the indictment. In the past six months, I have not been given any sort of legal assistance. An accused, defending himself out of detention and deprived of all other conditions enabling him to obtain what he needs to obtain, needs to have legal assistance, because my legal assistants have to be able to work out in the field and prepare my defence. I don't see how can you expect me to prepare my Defence on my own in my cell in those four walls with the paper that I have. You say, here, that I told you that I had understood my indictment. I only told you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- that I was given the indictment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- that I skimmed through it, and that it was on that basis that I plead. Even now, you are ---

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I'm going to stop you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- evading the territory that you--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please. Stop here for a moment. As I mentioned to you, I have dealt with the issue of language. What we were discussing, and what I want to go back to now, is the issues you raised regarding your health, and in particular issues that you have with the treatment at the UNDU. I don't wish to revisit, again, the issues that have been raised in your motions and decided upon, or deferred. Dealing first with the last point you were making on legal assistant, as I indicated earlier, I certainly appreciate the importance of the appointment of your legal counsel. I have looked very carefully at your submissions regarding legal assistant. I should say not legal counsel, because you are aware of the distinction between counsel and an assistant. But, as I mentioned earlier, this is a matter that has to be worked out initially with the registry. I have urged the registry, and I'm continuing to do so, to try and resolve that matter. So I appreciate how important that is; and, certainly, I would encourage you to continue those discussions with the registry. But that is a matter that primarily has to be dealt with, first of all, by the registry. Now, if we could go back to your points relating to the treatment in the UNDU. I can assure you, Mr. Tolimir, that I give -- I give careful consideration --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] French, French, French. I'm listening to French. I don't understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Can we check the channel, please, Madam Usher. I'm sorry. Are you receiving translation now, Mr. Tolimir, not in French, but in B/C/S? Are you hearing me now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes. Now I'm getting the translation in Serbo-Croatian. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Tolimir, I can assure you that we do, the Trial Chamber does give very careful consideration to all of the submissions that have you made. We have issued written decisions, in fact, by example, on the 10th of October, we did issue a written decision on your submissions regarding a violation of your rights. I'm not sure that you accepted service of that decision, Mr. Tolimir, but we certainly do give consideration to every submission that you make to us, and we respond to them when we require a decision from us. Some of them raised matters that aren't properly before the Trial Chamber. But certainly the decision of 10th October, by example, is a decision where we dealt with submissions you had made on the violation of your rights. So we are certainly prepared to do so, Mr. Tolimir. As I've mentioned previously, the matters obviously of your detention and the day-to-day supervision and activities is a matter that -- or is for the registry and the officials at the detention centre, and the Trial Chamber, of course, does not wish to interfere with the day-to-day administration, which is the responsibility of those bodies. However, I note that you have raised today, very clearly, the issue of the interruption of your sleep in the night, and the measures currently being used by the registry in terms of monitoring your condition. Without in any way interfering with their responsibilities in this regard, I will ask them to consider the matter and to consider what measures might be employed to be the least invasive, in terms of your sleep. So I will take up your point on this, Mr. Tolimir; and through -- through our legal officer, I will have some communications with the registry on that -- that particular point, because I note you have very clearly explained what your concerns are. So I will pursue those as best as possible, given the roles here in terms of administration. So I will certainly take that forward. I think you've made it very clear, as you have on previous occasions, that you -- your position regarding your health. The registry, again, being responsible for these matters, has made their position clear, and there really isn't much that the -- that I can do or the Chamber can do in that respect. I would, again, urge you to -- to take the medical advice that is being provided to you, and to follow that, Mr. Tolimir. As I say, I will follow up on the particular points you have raised. As to your latter comments, again, we're not going to revisit general issues, Mr. Tolimir, at this time. Are there any other -- I believe that was the specific issues I wished to deal with. Is there anything else you wish to raise, Mr. Tolimir? Again, we're not going to revisit the issue of language or service of documents at this time, but are there other issues that you wanted to raise this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there are. Thank you for allowing me to say that you are evading all questions that have to do with process and procedural actions. You are asking about the state of my health, which is excellent, but you are not concerned that I'm being prevented from receiving minimum legal assistance that I have a right to under Article 21 of the Statutes and Article 14 of the International Covenant on Human Rights. I have written five motions on this topic, and I have been writing motions on this, that I need to be given minimum legal assistance as a person defending themselves and is currently in detention. The registry does not wish to appoint legal advisors that I submitted. I did not wait for any deadlines to expire. I completed everything in the -- in the quickest possible deadline. I didn't wait in appointing my legal advisors, but the registry does not want to appoint my lawyers and advisors because it does not wish to me to represent myself. It is my fundamental right to represent myself and this cannot be delegated to somebody else, and this has to concern you as the Presiding Judge. In all laws, in all countries, members of the international community, and all laws and conventions that the Statute of the International Criminal Court is based on, agree that the accused can represent himself in his own mother tongue and in the language he understands and can read. You not wish to discuss this question which is the fundamental question, the most fundamental of all questions. I cannot be tried here. I cannot be denied the right to represent myself and to award this right to somebody else. No lawyer can receive documents unless I receive them first. When I receive them in the language and the script that I understand, only then can they be handed over to a lawyer. My documents cannot be disclosed to anyone else who would be possibly imposed on me, because in Article 21 it does not say that I can be imposed representation. It says that I can be appointed representation, but I cannot be given something that I'm not seeking. I'm not seeking representation. I'm just asking for legal assistants and for them to be paid. I have found my own legal assistants. So the registry provides for legal assistants to indigent persons who do not have the funds to cover that themselves. The International Tribunal can cover such costs if the accused are unable to cover those costs. I don't need legal assistants. I am choosing the legal assistants, and you just need to pay for that. The registry needs to pay for that, but you don't want to deal with that. That is the main question. I cannot carry out any activities in the field. From the detention unit, I cannot have any documents. I do not have any documents from other cases in order to acquaint myself with the jurisdiction of this Tribunal; and, constantly, you are referring to the jurisdiction. So I need to have all of these things, and only my legal assistants can prepare all of this. And for the past six months, I have not been allowed a minimum of legal assistance that I have a right to under the Statutes and under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights. I don't know why you are evading this question. This is the essential question. Why have my lawyers not been appointed as legal advisors, ones that I named on the 10th of October. That is two months ago, because it is already past the 10th of December. They have been representing Milan Martic for five years before this Tribunal. They have five years of experience before this Tribunal, more than perhaps some Judges who are members of the Trial Chamber. And according to them, the jurisdiction does not apply to them, and they cannot be elected because the registry does not wish to agree to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, let me stop you there. Unquestionably, and perhaps you weren't listening when I spoke earlier, I do accept the points that you have made, which you have made in writing and also orally, of your request for and need for legal assistance. Certainly, we have discussed the issue of your self-reputation on previous occasions. The registry has filed a submission, in which they have detailed the discussions that have been ongoing between you and them and your selected -- or the names that you have provided to them, and they have provided an explanation as to some of the reasons for the difficulties in actually concluding the appointment. You may not be aware of this in detail because have you not been accepting the filings, but there is a filing by the registry explaining this. No one, not the registry, nor the Trial Chamber, disputed your position that you wish to have legal assistants appointed and that you have identified individuals, but there are other factors such as whether the individuals in question are prepared to act for you, et cetera. I don't want to get into the it details of it again, because that is a primary responsibility of the registry. But it is not a matter which I am avoiding in any way, nor is it a matter that the registry from their submissions is voiding either. But there are ongoing matters that have to be resolved before the appointments can be finalised. Should the registry take a positive decision not to appoint someone and you wish to bring that forward, certainly you can bring that to us. But that has not been done to date. There is no decision on the part of the registry not to appoint a particular individual, so far as I'm aware from the filings to date. So I take the points, you've made your position very clear, and we will revisit this matter. Should there be any particular decisions taken, then certainly you can bring them to our attention, if you wish to. But at the moment what is important is that you look at the material the registry is providing you with, you discuss the matter with them, so that the appointment of your legal assistants can be carried out. So I'm going to leave that issue at that stage, Mr. Tolimir. I think your position is very clear on the record, and I again want to be very clear: My remarks earlier relating to self-reputation were tied very directly to the language issue. I think my comments were very clear, and that's where I'm going to leave the matter, Mr. Tolimir. So unless you have any other particular issues that you wish to discuss, as I say, the issue of legal assistants, I'm aware of your positions. I would urge you, and I am urging the registry, to conclude this matter as soon as possible with the appointment of a legal assistant that is of your choice, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but there is a crucial question that I would like to have recorded in the transcript, as you say. On several occasions, I asked for my legal advisors to be appointed, the ones that I proposed, in order to assistant me in conducting my Defence over the past six months; however, the registry keeps refusing. This is why I addressed you, as the Trial Chamber, as a control organ, to see why the secretariat is wasting my time for six months, because I didn't receive a single document or the minimum legal assistance that I have a right to under Article 21. I would like this Trial Chamber to see why I am being denied legal assistance in all possible options, from the beginning since I have come before the Tribunal until today. As a control organ, you need to see why somebody is obstructing and eating up my time that is it valuable for me for preparation, because six months have already gone by and I have not received a single document. I have not analysed it with my legal advisors who need to provide the minimum of legal assistance to me that I have a right to. So I would like to ask you to view this problem from that aspect and not to say that it is a problem of the registry. The Trial Chamber has just been reviewing my state of health. I don't understand that, and now you say that you will not discuss disclosure. It's not that I do not wish to receive the material. I cannot receive it, because if I do receive it, then the deadlines start running, the procedure starts running. I cannot receive something in a language that you consider that I know and that you would wish me to know, that you made up, and that was created after the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina. I cannot speak that language. I do not wish to learn it again. You would need to have a course here in Bosniak, Croatian, and Serbian. It is a new language, and here I'm only studying English. I'm not learning that Bosniak/Serbian/Croatian language that was created after the war. I would like you to keep this in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot accept that the language -- I cannot receive the documents because I don't understand the language. It's not that I don't want to, and I would like this to be entered into the transcript. I do not wish to enter into procedural actions with documents that I cannot read and cannot interpret. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Your position on the language issue is very clearly on the record, as is the decision that was rendered earlier. So we're not going to revisit that. As for the legal assistance, in closing, that issue for this afternoon, Mr. Tolimir, as I stated, the Registrar provided a submission outlining state of the discussions with you on the issue of your legal assistants. That is dated the 16th of November. It was served upon you, but I am -- I imagine it was amongst the documents that you did not agree to accept. So I certainly take your point. Your point is on the record, as I've indicated, as to your need on legal assistants. I'm sure the registry will be following the proceedings and will take note of your comments and of my request that they work to resolve this matter as soon as possible. Should it reach a point where any decision which, based on the material before me, there has not been, a positive decision on the part of anyone to deny you at this stage, the particular legal assistant that is being investigated or pursued, there's been no positive decision to say no to that request. If there is that, and you wish to bring it to your attention, certainly you can do so. But for the moment, I would please urge you to take a look at what the registry has set out in their submission of the 16th of November in that document, and I'm urging them, as well as you, to continue to work towards resolving the issue of legal assistants as soon as possible. But we will leave the matter there, and I have your point very clearly, that -- yes, Mr. Tolimir -- but, as I say, I don't wish to hear you again on the language issue, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You do not wish to discuss about things that are not authorised to discuss, and I understand that. I would just like to say that you need to understand that the registry does not want to resolve the question of my legal assistants, and the registry has not been talking with me for a month. They only had one conversation with me. You are saying that you are -- that I'm communicating with the registry, but I would like the transcript to reflect that I'm not communicating with the registry. I'm not talking with them. I don't what they're doing and what they want. You, as the Pre-Trial Judge, need to have this in mind. As the control organ, you need to see if any of the sides in the trial is being prejudiced. You do not wish to see here that I'm prejudiced, because the trial is conducted in a language and in a script that I don't understand. The problem here is that I cannot study a million pages of material in a language that I don't understand. My own Serbian language I learned. I learned to write in the Cyrillic. I'm writing like a person in the 4th grade, like a young boy, and you can see that by my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not wish to discuss any other things now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Please stop. We're not going to revisit the language issue, period. Now I have your points regarding discussions with the registry. I'm asking them to open again the discussions with you. If they have not spoken with you, I'm asking them to do so, and I'm asking you, on your part, to read the documentation that the registry has provided outlining the steps that they have taken regarding the appointment of your legal assistant, and we're going to end the matter there. I am inviting both the registry and you to engage again in discussions so that we can, as soon as possible, resolve the issue of your legal assistant. But we're not revisiting the issue of the language, and we won't discuss further this question. I think your position is very clear on the record, and I understand your position. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking you what the date of this document is. Secondly, I don't know the language the document is written in. I cannot read it, so could you please send somebody to read that for me or find a way. If I don't know the language, maybe somebody can read it to me. There is a translator. They can read that to me. I cannot read it. You can send hundreds of documents to me, but I don't know how to read. And this is why I cannot accept them because the procedural deadlines are running, and I cannot read the documents in a language that is not my mother tongue and that I did not learn. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, on this particular issue, I will invite the registry to communicate with you, to discuss with you, the content of that communication and their ongoing efforts to try and appoint your legal advisor. I will ask them to specifically do that, and we will leave it at that point. I hope that by the time of your next meeting, our next Status Conference, that the issue of your legal assistant will have been resolved. So I will ask the registry to follow up on that and to ensure that you're aware of their ongoing efforts and the status of that matter. I believe that is all of the issues. Mr. McCloskey, does the Prosecution have any particular issues it wished to raid this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Madam President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then barring any new issues, not the ones we have been discussing, but any new issues, I believe that covers all of the matters necessary for this afternoon's Status Conference. The next appearance will be communicated to you, Mr. Tolimir. Yes, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, I would like it to be recorded in the transcript that you and the Prosecution have the materials on the basis of which I'm being charged. I don't have the material. Only on the basis of the indictment that I read while I was still free, I know that I was charged just because I was the deputy commander of the Main Staff for Republika Srpska for Intelligence Affairs. I am only charged for being the deputy of Ratko Mladic. I am not ashamed of that. I'm proud of having been in the army under the command of Ratko Mladic. I would like to ask you to tell my why I am being charged and being held here for six months, so that I know, on the basis of which I can build my Defence. Other than that, there is no other charge other than that I was a soldier of the army of Republika Srpska, and the indictment was published openly on the web site of the Tribunal, and that is all I have read. I didn't even read the pre-trial motion. I would like to know what I'm being charged with, why I am here. If there is no other charge other than my being deputy commander of the -- commander of the army of Republika Srpska, then I ask to be allowed to go -- to be provisionally released and to be defended from freedom. I have nothing to fear, because all I am being charged with is of being the deputy of the commander of the army of Republika Srpska, Ratko Mladic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tolimir. Obviously, this Status Conference is not the time or place to go through the contents of the indictment in that respect. And in relation to any issues of provisional release, Mr. Tolimir, you have chosen to represent yourself, so those matters would have to be raised in the proper manner by way of proper motions for consideration; and, again, the Status Conference is not a time for consideration of those issues. So those matters are on the record now and they can be dealt with. But you've elected your own representation, so you have to bring them forward in accordance with the procedures of the Tribunal. And with that, there being no other matters before us, this proceeding is adjourned. Thank you, everyone. Have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: at 3.18 p.m.
